chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Abd al-Rahman said:

I asked him about a man who said to his slave: 'If an event befalls me, he is free, and upon the man is the freeing of a neck as expiation for an oath or for dhihar.' Is it permissible for him to emancipate the slave whom he designated for emancipation if an event befalls him, in the expiation of that oath? He said: 'It is not permissible for the one who designated that for him.'

key_terms.تَدْبِير: Manumission of a slave upon the master's death
key_terms.ظِهَار: A form of pre-Islamic/Islamic divorce where the husband likens the wife to his mother's back

ai.seo_question: Can a slave designated for emancipation upon death be used to fulfill the expiation for an oath or dhihar?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Aban ibn Taghlib clarifies the specific application of *tadbir* (manumission upon death) when designated as expiation (*kaffarah*) for an oath or *dhihar*. The ruling establishes that the emancipation of the specific slave serves as the fulfillment of the expiation obligation, thereby precluding the master from using that same slave for any other concurrent expiation requirement, highlighting the precision in Shia fiqh regarding conditional manumission and its legal consequences.
